newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - EU deepens probe of Siemens Elektrowatt buy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU deepens probe of Siemens Elektrowatt buy.

text.p: The European Commission began a full probe on Tuesday into Siemens AG's acquisition of part of Credit Suisse's stake in Elektrowatt saying it feared for competition in the markets for electricity meters and payphones.
A decision to start an in-depth probe into a deal usually means the companies involved may have to make concessions to win EU regulatory approval. A final ruling will take up to four months.

Credit Suisse, one of Switzerland's largest banks, announced earlier this year it was selling most of its 44.9-percent holding in Elektrowatt, another Swiss company active in the energy sector and which also provides services and systems for utilities and makes payphones and visual security devices.

Siemens agreed to buy the industrial activities while a consortium of Swiss and German power companies, including Bayernwerk, would acquire the energy part of Elektrowatt. The Commission's current probe does not concern the energy deal.

Following an initial one-month probe, the Commission said that Siemens and Elektrowatt together could control 50 percent or more of the affected markets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Denmark, the Netherlands and Austria.
It was particularly concerned about the impact on electricity meters, a market traditionally controlled by a small number of powerful companies. Schlumberger is another big producer of meters.

"On the (European) level, it cannot be excluded at this time that a joint dominant position of Siemens/Elektrowatt and Schlumberger for electricity meters can be created through the merger," the Commission said in a statement.
It noted that Siemens and the Swiss company would also have more than 40 percent of the market for payphones in Germany, but it needed to assess the competitive situation further.

"The main concerns of the Commission are the high market shares of the parties for electricity meters, highly concentrated markets even before the merger, and for payphones in Germany," the statement said.

The Commission has the power under the European Union's merger control law to impose conditions before approving any mergers and takeovers found to create or strengthen dominant positions in the 15-nation market.

It has blocked eight such deals since 1990 when it became the EU's clearing house for all deals involving companies with a combined worldwide turnover of five billion European currency units and EU sales of at least 250 million Ecus each.
Siemens's planned purchase of the industrial activities of Elektrowatt AG was filed to the Commission for clearance on June 24.
